notes: wstETH itself is immutable (no owner, no proxy): every power on this card is over stETH, its rate path and the bridges.

Lido DAO path: Aragon Agent → Dual Governance Admin Executor → EmergencyProtectedTimelock; proposals come only from the Aragon Voting (LDO). Shortest path to execution: 5 d vote + 3 d after submit (+1 d after schedule unless the Emergency Execution Committee executes in emergency mode); stETH holders can extend it (veto signalling).
Aragon votes (the days before a proposal reaches Dual Governance) are not read: a change appears here once it is submitted to Dual Governance.
History before block 17,600,000 is not scanned, except the Aragon ACL (read from 2020 to know who holds each permission; those rows are replayed, not listed).
The canonical rollup bridges' own message verification (proof systems, sequencers, rollup security councils) is not read. Linea's TokenBridge is Linea-run, not Lido's.
Not covered: Polygon PoS and third-party bridges (other OFTs / wrappers), the Tiebreaker committee internals, and the first Dual Governance contract (0xcdf49b05…, replaced 2025-09).

The L2 side of each canonical bridge (the L2 wstETH token and bridge, upgraded on each L2 by Lido's cross-chain governance executor) is not read: on Ethereum, each bridge's upgrade path, switches and locked balance are. The Wormhole NTT route is read on BOTH sides at head (the BNB Chain manager's threshold, transceivers, owner, pauser and wstETH supply, through public RPCs); the BNB Chain side's event history is not scanned, and its owner is classified on BNB Chain only (a cross-chain governance executor there is not followed back to the Lido DAO).
The NTT Axelar transceiver has no peer getter: its peers come from AxelarChainIdSet events (history), not a head read.
Redemption: the WithdrawalQueue (stETH → ETH) is read for its pause switch and upgrade path; its role grants (who may pause or resume withdrawals) are replayed from block 17,600,000.
